title: Say it. Shape it.
summary: An original chat-driven design recording becomes a focused software promo with exact typography, readable UI crops, and explicit editable source cuts.

inputs.label: Original Forma recording
inputs.description: A 12-second original scripted fixture: a chat request creates a garden landing page and a follow-up warms its palette. This fictional interface does not claim shipping-product behavior.

inputs.label: Exact copy and focus hints
inputs.description: Supplied product name, exact titles, colors, timestamp hints, and named source regions. The workflow preserves this wording and the actual recording pixels.

stages.label: Inspect the recording
stages.description: Validate the source and sample its chronology before any paid call.

stages.label: Refine a saved editable plan
stages.description: An image-aware structured model proposed the original camera plan. The caller authored four chronological source intervals and revised camera beat times to remove waits and hold the visible results; exact source pixels and brief remain unchanged.

stages.label: Render exact source pixels
stages.description: Local typography and camera framing render the saved plan at $0. Explicit cuts retain the completed requests and outcomes. Strict full-file decoding validates the delivered MP4.

stages.label: Independent sampled review
stages.description: A different model accepted all eight criteria on timestamped frames, the full-size poster, exact-copy brief, and report.

outputs.label: Independent editorial review of exact selected bytes

stages.label: Apply the utility to a denser browser recording
stages.description: A different original 44-second browser recording supplies a table, a dashboard request and a returning-customers refinement. Model-selected chronological intervals omit long waits; the caller repaired the filename crop and source chart alignment before exact-output review. The 19-second saved-plan replay remains local and free.

outputs.label: Dashboard exact-copy brief and focus hints
Selected intervals and disclosed crop repair
Dashboard source intervals and structural report
Independent editorial review of repaired exact bytes
Complete additional-study inputs and stage manifest

limitations: This original fictional recording is a separate fixture generator; callers supply prepared, rights-cleared footage of their own product.

One silent 1920 × 1080 composition with explicit chronological source intervals. Caller-approved cuts omit waits and independently retime retained footage; narration, sound design, device mockups and larger edits remain outside this utility.
Independent review covers sampled visual evidence and a static poster, not continuous motion or listening. Source and final MP4 decoding are structural checks.
The same workflow also produced independently reviewed original poster-design and dense dashboard recordings. A few inputs are transfer evidence, not a general success rate.
